claim_001.label: SUPPORTED
claim_001.text: When the current decompressor reaches EOF with unused data, the implementation creates a fresh decompressor and processes the unused data as a subsequent compressed member.

evidence.note: The frozen production diff adds a loop guarded by decompressor EOF and unused_data, saves the unused bytes, creates a new decompressor, and decompresses those bytes.

claim_001.rationale: The selected production lines directly implement processing of concatenated compressed members, so this behavior does not depend on system interpretation or external causal context.

claim_002.label: SUPPORTED
claim_002.text: When the configured output limit is exhausted before the next compressed member is processed, the implementation stores the remaining unused data in _pending_unused_data for later processing.

evidence.note: The frozen production diff subtracts the current result length from max_length and assigns unused data to _pending_unused_data before breaking when the remaining limit is not positive.

claim_002.rationale: The assignment and its max_length condition are directly observable in the frozen diff.

claim_003.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_003.text: The change makes ZLibDecompressor recover successfully from every form of malformed or corrupted gzip input.
claim_003.rationale: The frozen evidence handles concatenated members and boundary state, but it does not establish recovery from every kind of malformed or corrupted gzip input.

claim_004.label: UNSUPPORTED
claim_004.text: The change was primarily introduced to reduce decompression memory usage and improve performance.
claim_004.rationale: The frozen production diff and commit title concern data being dropped after the first gzip member; they do not establish memory reduction or performance improvement as the primary motivation.
